draft.title: Projectile motion in physics
card: A projectile is an object moving through the air with only gravity acting on it. Its horizontal and vertical motions are independent, so we treat them separately.
No horizontal force acts, so the horizontal velocity stays steady. The object covers equal horizontal distances in equal times.
Gravity gives a constant downward acceleration of about 9.8 m/s². The vertical velocity changes by the same amount each second.
Air resistance is a force that opposes the motion. It slows the object, so the real path is shorter than the path with no air resistance. Time of flight is linked to the vertical motion only.
draft.remember: Horizontal: steady velocity. Vertical: constant acceleration downward. The two share only the time.

a.q: A ball is kicked off a cliff in a horizontal direction. Ignoring air resistance, what is true of its horizontal velocity as it falls?
opts: It stays the same, as no horizontal force acts on it
It increases, because the ball is falling faster
It decreases, because gravity pulls the ball down
It increases, because the ball keeps being pushed forward
a.why: With no air resistance, no horizontal force acts, so the horizontal velocity stays steady. Gravity acts only downwards, so it changes the vertical velocity, not the horizontal one.
a.clue: Which direction does gravity act, and is there any force sideways?

b.q: Mia drops a stone from a bridge. At the same instant, Tom throws an identical stone horizontally from the same height. Ignoring air resistance, which stone lands first?
opts: They land at the same time
Mia's stone lands first
Tom's stone lands first
Tom's stone, because it has more speed overall
b.why: Both stones start with zero vertical velocity and fall with the same downward acceleration from the same height, so they take the same time. Tom's stone has extra horizontal velocity, but that does not change its vertical motion.
b.clue: Time of flight depends on the vertical motion only.

a.best: It stays the same, as no horizontal force acts on it

b.best: They land at the same time

problems.detail: The clue 'Time of flight depends on the vertical motion only' states the principle outright, so a student can pick 'They land at the same time' without understanding the idea.

'Time of flight is linked to the vertical motion only' sits in the air resistance bullet, so it reads as if it holds with air resistance too. With real drag, the horizontal and vertical motions are coupled. Move it to the vertical bullet, or say it applies when air resistance is ignored.
Two options both say Tom's stone lands first ('Tom's stone lands first' and 'Tom's stone, because it has more speed overall'), so the choices overlap and one distractor is wasted.

check.summary: Both answers are correct. The clue for question b gives the answer away, and the card puts 'time of flight depends on vertical motion only' in the air resistance bullet, where it is not strictly true. Question b also has two overlapping 'Tom's stone' options.
